title: Registration data interception during account creation
description: Homeowner's registration information (personal identifiers, device details) could be intercepted during transmission to the Home Hub, potentially exposing sensitive personal data to unauthorized parties.

title: Information leakage during device enrollment
description: Personal information about the homeowner and their enrolled cameras/sensors could be leaked during the enrollment process, potentially revealing location data, device types, and usage patterns.

title: Unauthorized access to registration data
description: The Home Hub could be accessed by unauthorized parties during the registration process, potentially allowing them to view or modify the homeowner's account information and enrolled devices.

title: Registration data integrity compromise
description: The registration data and device enrollment information could be tampered with during processing, potentially leading to incorrect account setup or unauthorized device access.

title: Access Code Leaking During Entry
description: Guest's temporary access code may be leaked during entry process (e.g., visible on screen, spoken aloud, logged in plaintext), potentially exposing the guest's identity or access credentials to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Access via Weak Code
description: Guest may attempt to use weak or guessed access codes to gain unauthorized access to the front door, bypassing intended security controls.

title: Inability to Detect Unauthorized Access Attempts
description: Home Hub may not effectively detect or log unauthorized access attempts, making it difficult to identify security breaches or suspicious behavior.

title: Unintended Door Access Consequences
description: Temporary access code may result in unintended consequences such as door being unlocked when it shouldn't be, or access granted to unauthorized persons.

title: Data Loss During Storage
description: Motion/door/sensor events written to the local event log may be lost due to storage corruption, power failure, or system crash, resulting in incomplete event records.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log is a persistent storage mechanism that can experience storage failures.

title: Unauthorized Access to Event Log
description: An unauthorized actor may gain access to the local event log and read or modify motion/door/sensor events without proper authorization.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log is accessible to other system components or users.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Data
description: Motion/door/sensor events stored in the local event log may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or data leakage.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log may be accessible to external or unauthorized entities.

title: Unintended Data Flow from Event Log
description: Motion/door/sensor events stored in the local event log may be inadvertently accessed or transmitted to unintended recipients or systems.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log may be integrated with other systems that could access its contents.

title: Regulatory Compliance for Personal Data Storage
description: Storing motion/door/sensor events in the local event log may violate privacy regulations or data protection requirements for handling personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the local event log may contain personal data subject to privacy regulations.

title: Data Loss During Upload
description: Camera clip data may be lost during the upload process from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage due to network failures, server crashes, or transmission errors.

title: Unauthorized Access During Upload
description: Unauthorized parties may intercept or access camera clip data during the upload process from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage.

title: Data Destruction During Storage
description: Camera clip data may be destroyed or corrupted during storage in Cloud Video Storage due to system failures, hardware issues, or malicious attacks.

title: Unintended Data Access
description: Camera clip data may be accessed by unintended parties or systems during storage in Cloud Video Storage without proper authorization controls.

title: Motion notification may disclose sensitive home activity information
description: The motion-detected notification sent to the homeowner may reveal sensitive information about when and where the homeowner is present or absent from their home, potentially exposing privacy-sensitive patterns of behavior.
assumptions: The notification includes details about motion detection location and timing that could be inferred to reveal homeowner presence/absence patterns.

title: Homeowner lacks control over notification timing and frequency
description: The homeowner may not have granular control over when motion notifications are sent, potentially receiving notifications at inconvenient times or with excessive frequency.
assumptions: The mobile app backend controls notification scheduling without sufficient homeowner customization options.

title: Notification may contain more information than necessary
description: The motion notification may include unnecessary or excessive information beyond what is required for the notification purpose, such as detailed location data or timestamps.
assumptions: The notification includes more data than the minimum required to convey the motion detection event.

title: Notification may be sent to unintended recipient
description: The motion notification may be sent to the wrong homeowner or to multiple homeowners when only one should receive it, due to system configuration errors or data mapping issues.
assumptions: The notification system may have errors in recipient identification or may broadcast to multiple users.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be retained longer than necessary for the intended purpose, violating the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: Assumes video retention policy exceeds minimum required retention period
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Retention policies may vary by jurisdiction and use case; this is a general assessment based on typical cloud storage practices.

title: Violation of storage security principle
description: Video data stored in cloud storage may not be adequately protected against unauthorized access, data breaches, or security incidents.
assumptions: Assumes cloud storage provider security controls may be insufficient or misconfigured
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Cloud provider security posture varies; this assessment assumes potential vulnerabilities in storage security controls.

title: Unintended access to video data
description: Mobile app backend may expose video data to unauthorized users or systems during retrieval and playback process.
assumptions: Assumes authentication/authorization controls may be bypassed or misconfigured
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Access controls depend on implementation; this is a general assessment of potential vulnerabilities.

title: Data destruction during playback
description: Video data may be improperly destroyed or corrupted during the retrieval and playback process by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes data handling procedures may not properly manage data lifecycle
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Data destruction procedures vary by implementation; this is a general assessment of potential vulnerabilities.
